This is the original source. It lists 13 schools:

Achievement Academy

This is a public adult high school. This is designed to pick up people who couldn't finish high school. This is expected.

Carver Vocational-Technical High

This is a VoTech school, with an enrollment of about 900 students.

Excel Acadamy @ Francis M. Wood High

(SIC) This is a public adult high school with an enrollment of about 300. This is for idiots, and so it is not surprising for zero students here to be proficient in math.

Forest Park High

This is a standard High School with an enrollment of about 500 students. This is in line with the narrative of the article.

Frederick Douglass High

This is a standard High School with an enrollment of about 900 students. This is in line with the narrative of the article.

Independence School Local 1

This is a charter school, run by someone with a Ph.D. in something. The enrollment is 127. It's part of a learning initiative, so it's expected that they'd take on large numbers of bad students.

Knowledge and Success Academy

I went to their site: the name is actually "Knowledge Achievement Success Academy". That's pretty bad. I'm not looking into them too much, but everything I found so far looks horrifying.

New Era Academy

This is a charter school with mixed middle school and high school students, with an enrollment of about 400. It's labelled as a gimmicky high school of some sort, but that wouldn't explain the given level of failure.

New Hope Academy

As with KASA, I couldn't find much on these guys, but what I found was bad.

Northwestern High

The school is listed as "defunct" by wikipedia, as of May of 2017. It was a typical high school, and fits the narrative of the article.

Patterson High

This is a typical high school with enrollment of about 1000. This fits the narrative of the article.

The Reach! Partnership School

This is a school marketed at failures.

Of the 13 schools listed in the article, then, we have that:

  • 4 of these are not surprising.
  • 5 of these fit with the narrative of the article perfectly.
  • 1 of these shut down, and thus it is not fair to make a judgement based on it.
  • 2 of these I didn't find enough data on for me to judge.

Coppin Academy

Coppin Academy is affiliated with a Public University - Coppin State University. In other words, these students are getting probably the best possible help they could reasonably get - help that money cannot buy!

The superintendent has a Ph.D. We might be able to chalk this up to poor management, but that seems like a long stretch.

This is perhaps the quintessential case study that argues that pumping up funding and giving resources to certain groups of students may be utterly futile, even if those resources are so invaluable that they cannot be purchased.
